title: Comparing and Evaluating Changepoint Methods with ggchangepoint
text: single changepoint detection method dominates across signal shapes, noise regimes, computational budgets: large-scale evaluations find ranking algorithms highly dataset-dependent default configurations often far optimal (van den Burg Williams 2020; Truong et al. 2020). Sound practice therefore requires running several detectors, comparing outputs, — ground truth available — scoring well-defined accuracy metrics. article presents comparison evaluation toolkit ggchangepoint: visual comparison across methods (ggcpt_compare()), common tidy representation competing segmentations (ggcpt_compare_table()), metrics module implementing precision/recall/F1 one--one matching, covering metric, Hausdorff distance, adjusted Rand index (cpt_metrics()), multi-annotator scoring style Turing Change Point Dataset benchmark (cpt_metrics_annotated()), visual evaluation ground truth (ggcpt_eval()). discuss three complementary tools quantifying uncertainty segmentation — engine-native confidence intervals, bootstrap stability profiles (cpt_stability()), CROPS penalty path (cpt_crops()) — close small simulation-based benchmarking workflow built package’s ground-truth generators.

title: Comparing and Evaluating Changepoint Methods with ggchangepoint
text: changepoint literature offers wide menu detectors — penalised optimal partitioning, binary segmentation wild narrowest--threshold refinements, moving-sum statistics, nonparametric divergence measures, Bayesian posteriors — inductive bias (Aminikhanghahi Cook 2017; Truong et al. 2020). Benchmarks score many algorithms many series find uniform winner: performance depends kind change (mean, variance, distribution), noise (Gaussian, heavy-tailed, autocorrelated), number spacing changes, tuning penalties thresholds (van den Burg Williams 2020). Two practical consequences follow. First, analyst compare several methods data hand rather trust one default. Second, ground truth (expert annotation) exists, comparison quantitative, using metrics agreed conventions. ggchangepoint supports activities behind one interface. Every detector returns tidy ggcpt object, competing methods directly comparable; comparison module renders side side, evaluation module scores . article package’s methods-paper treatment workflow. companion vignette vignette("introduction", package = "ggchangepoint") documents full detection surface; take detectors given focus comparison, evaluation, uncertainty.

text: package provides composable ggplot2 layers changepoint visualisation:
code: library(ggplot2)  # Use geom_changepoint as a standalone layer cp_tbl <- tidy(cpt_detect(x, method = "pelt", change_in = "mean")) ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   geom_changepoint(data = cp_tbl, aes(xintercept = cp), color = "red") +   theme_ggcpt()  # Use stat_changepoint to compute and draw changepoints in one step ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   stat_changepoint(method = "pelt", color = "red")  # Shade alternating segments between changepoints ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   annotate_segments(cp = cp_tbl$cp, n = length(x))  # Draw each segment's estimated level with geom_cpt_segment segs <- cpt_detect(x, method = "pelt", change_in = "mean")$segments ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   geom_cpt_segment(data = segs,                    aes(x = start, xend = end,                        y = param_estimate, yend = param_estimate),                    color = "blue", linewidth = 1)  # Draw confidence intervals with geom_cpt_ci (when the engine provides them) cp_ci <- tidy(smuce_wrapper(x)) ggplot(data.frame(index = seq_along(x), value = x), aes(index, value)) +   geom_line() +   geom_cpt_ci(data = cp_ci,               aes(x = cp, xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper, y = min(x) - 1))

title: ggchangepoint package — ggchangepoint-package
text: ggchangepoint provides consistent S3 result class (ggcpt) changepoint detection results, broom-style methods (tidy(), glance(), augment()), ggplot2 integration via autoplot() composable geoms (geom_changepoint(), geom_cpt_segment(), geom_cpt_ci(), stat_changepoint()), unified dispatcher cpt_detect() supports thirty methods. **Detection engines.** cpt_detect() currently dispatches 31 methods across six families (run cpt_methods() live table installation status): Penalised/optimal: PELT, BinSeg, SegNeigh, AMOC     (changepoint); FPOP (fpop); CROPS penalty path     (cpt_crops()); fastcpd (fastcpd, incl. AR/ARMA/GARCH);     change--slope via CPOP (cpop). Multiscale/search: WBS (wbs), WBS2 TGUH     (breakfast), (), MOSUM incl. multiscale     (mosum), Isolate-Detect (IDetect), SMUCE/HSMUCE     confidence intervals (stepR). Nonparametric/kernel: NP (changepoint.np),     E-Divisive/E-Agglo (ecp), kernel running statistics     (kcpRS), NP-MOJO (CptNonPar), sequential CPM (cpm),     self-normalisation (SNSeg). Bayesian: Barry-Hartigan posterior (bcp), online     BOCPD (ocp), BEAST model averaging (Rbeast). Multivariate/high-dimensional: sparse projection     (InspectChangepoint), online ocd (ocd), geometric mapping     (changepoint.geo). Regression breaks robust detection: Bai-Perron breaks     CIs (strucchange), broken-line regression     (segmented), changepoints-vs-autocorrelation model selection     (EnvCpt), drift+AR robust detection (DeCAFS). **Key features.** Every detector returns ggcpt object stable tibble(cp, cp_value) contract (plus engine extras ci_lower/ci_upper posterior_prob). Visualise result directly autoplot() (confidence intervals, fitted signals, multivariate facets), Bayesian displays (ggcpt_posterior(), ggcpt_runlength()), interactively via ggcpt_interactive(). Compare methods ggcpt_compare(); run panels series cpt_batch(); quantify uncertainty cpt_stability(); sweep penalties cpt_crops(). Evaluate accuracy cpt_metrics() ggcpt_eval(); simulate ground-truth data cpt_simulate() canonical test signals; cite methodology behind result cpt_cite().
